meta.comment: engine.traffic (planned MOD) inc0 table (h): parking demand per trip end by land use, kerb vs off-street split, turnover. data/roads.json already carries a boolean 'parking' flag per road class (kerb parking permitted y/n) -- referenced, not restated; this file adds the DEMAND side.
meta.unitsConvention: spacesPerTripEnd = parking spaces demanded per non-home trip end (dimensionless ratio); turnoverPerDay = average number of distinct vehicles using one space per day; footprintM2 cross-references vehicle_classes.json parkingFootprintM2 (not restated).

dwelling_low_density.note: off-street driveway/garage the norm at low density
dwelling_low_density.source: UK planning standard order-of-magnitude (residential parking standards vary by local authority; 1.5-2.0 spaces/dwelling is a common suburban norm)

dwelling_high_density.note: reduced parking standard typical of dense/transit-served development
dwelling_high_density.source: UK planning standard order-of-magnitude (many UK city-centre residential parking standards cap at <1 space/unit)

office_job.source: derived approximation (city-centre office parking ratios commonly well below 1:1 in UK planning practice)

school_pupil.note: staff parking only; pupil drop-off is kerbside, not parked

kerbVsOffStreet.$comment: Split of a class's total parking DEMAND (from demandByLandUse) between on-street/kerb spaces and off-street (surface lot / multi-storey) supply, by density band -- higher density pushes parking off-street due to kerb space scarcity and land-value pressure toward structured parking.
kerbVsOffStreet.source: derived approximation, informed by observed kerb-space scarcity/structured-parking prevalence gradient in dense cities (Tokyo/Singapore/central London order-of-magnitude pattern)

offStreetCommuter.note: office/industrial commuter lot, ~one user/day plus rare second use

offStreetRetail.note: shopping centre multi-storey, high daily turnover

provenance.source: UK local-authority residential/commercial parking standard orders of magnitude, own derived approximations for turnover and kerb/off-street split
provenance.note: No published single UK national parking-standard table exists (standards are locally set); every figure here is a directional cross-authority order-of-magnitude, pending Aaron's balance pass.
